_doc: Hub conversations. Each NPC's list is checked in order; the first entry whose 'if' conditions all hold is used. Conditions: 'flag' (set), '!flag' (not set), 'stat>=n' / 'stat<n' on Profile.stats (runs, deaths, clears, best_depth, shards_found, tm_earned). 'set' lists flags to set when the conversation ends. 'then': 'restore' opens the restoration menu afterwards. Lines are [speaker, text]; speaker is an NPC id, or 'system' for game notices.

lines: Forgive an old man for staring. It has been a while since anyone logged in. Weeks? The clock tower stopped counting.
The notice went up at midnight. 'Service has ended. Thank you for playing.' And then, one by one, everyone simply... stopped.
Something is wrong past the gate. Coral Beach keeps resetting itself, and the monsters wake angrier every time.
Someone who can still leave the square might see why. The gate is just north of the fountain. And do come back. Please.
Something curious happened when you came back. The character select screen flickered.
A second slot. A Bunny, waiting by the gate, fists up. Somebody's old character, or a new one of yours?
Choose at the gate. The city remembers you either way.
You came back! I watched the beach fold up like a map, and the whole world... rewound.
We call it a rollback. When it happens, the city forgets the last few hours. Usually.
But I remember you leaving. That shouldn't be possible.
Bring back what you find out there. Time Marks, shards. The city keeps what you carry home. Perhaps together we can mend a few things.
The Golden Mole, beaten? So that's why the lights steadied for a moment.
Every time you push back the rot out there, a little more of the world holds together. I felt the fountain run warm.
Coral Beach is only the edge of it. But it's a start. Let's see how long we can keep the lights on.
Ah, my favourite player. My only player, but still my favourite. What shall we mend today?
Oh! A customer! Wait. Are you real? Not one of the echoes?
Sorry. Since the notice, the square fills up with shapes that look like players. They walk the old routes, then fade.
The shop's closed, I'm afraid. No suppliers, no customers. Just me and a lot of potions nobody needs.
This will sound strange, but... did you die today?
I dreamt of sand and a golden mole, and then everything snapped back like a rubber band. You were there.
Nobody remembers the rollbacks. So why do I?
If the shop ever reopens, you get the first discount. Being the only customer has its perks.
Shh. Look up. Count them with me.
Every star up there is a world like ours. A server. Every night there are fewer.
When a star goes out, it doesn't fall. It just... isn't.
You're carrying a Harkon Shard. Can you feel it hum?
It's warm the way the sky used to be. I think it's a piece of our star that refuses to go out.
Bring them home. If enough of them gather here, maybe the light holds.
SERVICE TERMINATION NOTICE. This world will end service at 00:00. All data will be deleted. Thank you for playing.
Someone has scratched a line under the notice: 'Not yet.'
SERVICE TERMINATION NOTICE. This world will end service at 00:00. All data will be deleted. Thank you for playing.
Oh! A customer. Sorry, sorry. I was talking to the keys again.
Keeper Julio, Megalopolis Warehouse. Every player's storage, all of it, still here. Nobody came to collect.
The server rolls back whatever you carry when you fall out there. But what reaches my shelves stays put. I checked. Twice.
Find a Portable Port past the gate and send me something good. Next time you head out, take it back off the shelf. An heirloom, if you like.
Fair warning: Coral Beach is a low-level area. The server syncs your gear down there, so a +9 sword swings like a +3.
It arrived! Shelf one, row one. First new item in this warehouse since the shutdown.
Your shelves, as you left them.
The stall's open? It's open! Compounder Paul, at your service. Again. Finally.
Out there every monster drops a little something. Cool Ice from the penguins, Sharp Legs from the Bad Furies, Hard Scales off the Bustshells.
Bring enough of one kind to a Compounder and it'll set it into your gear's slot. The numbers roll, mind. That's half the fun.
Doors past the gate name the monsters behind them now. Pick the den with the material you need.
Leftover materials end up with me now. Pick a stored piece and we'll set something in it.
Hm. The forge is warm again. You did that?
Marx. Blacksmith. I don't talk much. The anvil talks.
You'll find gear out there now, and anvils. Bring Bronze Fragments and Galder. Refining past +4 bites back, so mind your luck.
Shops are open too. Mostly mine.
Bring me what's on Julio's shelves. Banked Galder, banked Bronze. The anvil does the rest.
You found the support desk! Guide Sabrina. I was the last of the staff on shift when the lights went out.
The GMs left their console unlocked. I shouldn't touch it. I've been touching it.
I can make the server harder on you. Heavier load, laggier monsters, PK on. The harder it gets, the more TM sticks to you.
And every time you clear at a new best Heat, I'll slip you a Harkon Shard for each level. Our secret.
Console's warm. What are we breaking today?
A card hunter's work is never done. Even after the end of the world. Especially after.
Every monster out there carries a card, if you hit it right. Bring them home and they go in my album.
Finish a page and I'll give you something from my collection to wear. Ears, tails, the good stuff.
Or buy, if you're impatient. I take Time Marks. I'm not proud.
Hah! A student. I'd started teaching the pigeons.
Master Louis. Power techniques are my art. Shockwave, Lacerator, all of it.
Every run you log in knowing nothing. Bring me what the monsters drop, and one technique walks out of the gate with you.
A technique learns from the monster that tests it. Penguin ice, scorpion stings. Bring more, and it leaves sharper.
Stance. Breath. Show me what you brought.
Shop's open! Driller Marky! Drills, drills and more drills!
Take a Basic Drill, on the house. Find a Dig Site out there and hit the ground when the marker's in the green.
Gold zone in the middle digs half again. Miss too often and you'll wake something that lives down there.
Basic gets you ore and bits. Want gear and Harkon Shards? You'll need to dig deeper. I sell deeper.
Deeper is better! What'll it be?
